title: Data Augmentation
oneLine: Manufacture label-preserving variety to regularize a vision model.

paras: A flipped, rotated, or cropped cat is still a cat. Augmentation applies these label-preserving transforms during training so the model sees far more variety than the raw dataset holds, teaching invariance to nuisance factors and curbing overfitting - the cheapest regularizer in vision.
Train on transformed inputs whose label is unchanged:
sections.texNote: T is sampled fresh each epoch; the family T encodes which variations should not change the label.

sections.code:
import numpy as np

def augment(img):
    if np.random.rand() < 0.5: img = img[:, ::-1]      # h-flip
    img = np.roll(img, np.random.randint(-3, 4), axis=0) # shift
    return img
sections.caption: Fresh random transforms each epoch multiply the effective data.

takeaways: Augmentation adds label-preserving variety for free.
It teaches invariance and reduces overfitting.
Strong augmentation underpins modern self-supervised vision.
